steps.ask: Which angles are equal because of the parallel lines? What is the reason for each?
steps.title: Find two pairs of equal angles

lines.text: $PA \parallel BR$, so $|\angle HBQ| = |\angle HAP|$. Reason: alternate angles.
$|\angle QHB| = |\angle PHA|$. Reason: vertically opposite angles.

steps.ask: How many pairs of equal angles do you need before two triangles are similar?
steps.title: Conclude the triangles are similar

lines.text: Two angles are equal, so $\triangle AHP$ and $\triangle BHQ$ are equiangular, hence similar.

steps.ask: Which side of triangle BHQ corresponds to AH, and which to AP? Write the ratio.
steps.title: Write the ratio of corresponding sides

lines.text: $A \leftrightarrow B$ and $H \leftrightarrow H$, so $AH$ corresponds to $BH$ and $AP$ corresponds to $BQ$.
Corresponding sides of similar triangles are proportional: $\dfrac{\hl{2}{|AH|}}{\hl{4}{|HB|}} = \dfrac{\hl{3}{|AP|}}{|QB|}$.

steps.ask: What do you multiply both sides by to clear the fractions?
steps.title: Cross-multiply

lines.text: Multiply both sides by $|HB|\,|QB|$: $\hl{1}{|AH| \times |QB| = |AP| \times |HB|}$.
